key_insight: Loading classical data into superconducting quantum computers has a substantial dynamic energy cost that depends on QRAM architecture, control settings, and refrigeration attenuation.
engineering_relevance: At fixed target fidelity, optimizing operating conditions and attenuation distribution can change average dynamic power by a factor of two or more.
method: Model QRAM fidelity and power using a metric-noise-resource framework that includes thermal photons and gate errors.
Analyze linear-depth multiplexer and bucket-brigade architectures.
Adapt bucket-brigade QRAM to native superconducting gates and evaluate its fully decomposed schedule.
evidence_signal: For a modeled bucket-brigade query with a 12-qubit address register, the authors report 0.969 fidelity, 3.51×10⁻⁴ J dynamic energy, 4.38 W average dynamic power, and 64.4 W peak dynamic power.
watch_item: These model-based dynamic-cost estimates do not establish experimentally measured performance or total system energy consumption.
paper_title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
